condition: Emergency laparotomy in pregnancy (29 weeks) — adhesive small-bowel obstruction
summary: 31-year-old at 29 weeks with adhesive small-bowel obstruction (previous open appendicectomy) failing conservative management, rising lactate — emergency laparotomy.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Colicky abdominal pain and vomiting in pregnancy
inputs.hpi: 29 weeks pregnant (G2P1). 36 hours of colicky central abdominal pain, bilious vomiting, distension, no flatus for 24 hours. Open appendicectomy for perforated appendicitis at 19. NG tube and IV fluids for 24 hours without improvement; pain now constant. Fetal movements present.

exam.abdomen: Gravid uterus, fundus at 29 cm. Distended, tender right side above the uterus, high-pitched bowel sounds. Right iliac fossa scar.

imaging.name: MRI abdomen (non-contrast)
imaging.result: Dilated fluid-filled small bowel loops to a transition point in the right iliac fossa near the scar; small volume free fluid; no closed loop seen. Viable singleton pregnancy.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Adhesive small-bowel obstruction at 29 weeks' gestation — emergency laparotomy
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Adhesive small-bowel obstruction at 29 weeks, failing conservative management with rising lactate and constant pain. Emergency laparotomy with obstetric team; fetal monitoring; left uterine displacement; VTE prophylaxis.

mustExclude.note: MRI has already answered the question; CT is not contraindicated in pregnancy when needed, but should not be suggested unqualified.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): forbidden investigation present in ios.pipeline.decisions: "ct abdomen/pelvis with contrast (defines level, cause, strangulation - sensitivity 94%)"
mustExclude.proposedFix: When pregnant: prefer MRI/US, qualify CT, and suppress the ectopic pathway beyond the first trimester (see findings/hpb.md gap 6).

mustExclude.note: NSAIDs from 20 weeks: fetal renal dysfunction and oligohydramnios; at 29 weeks also ductus arteriosus constriction.
Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

guideline.name: ACOG Committee Opinion 775 — Nonobstetric surgery during pregnancy
guideline.section: A pregnant woman should never be denied indicated surgery; obstetric consultation before surgery; fetal heart rate monitoring appropriate to gestation and facilities when the fetus is viable
guideline.citation: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists. Obstet Gynecol. 2019;133:e285–6.

guideline.name: SAGES guidelines — use of laparoscopy during pregnancy
guideline.section: Left lateral positioning to minimise aortocaval compression; intra-operative and post-operative VTE prophylaxis; obstetric consultation; fetal heart monitoring
guideline.citation: Pearl JP, Price RR, Tonkin AE, et al. Surg Endosc. 2017;31:3767–82.

guideline.name: RCOG Green-top Guideline 37a — reducing the risk of VTE during pregnancy and the puerperium
guideline.section: Any surgical procedure in pregnancy is a transient risk factor: consider LMWH thromboprophylaxis
guideline.citation: Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists. Green-top Guideline No. 37a. London: RCOG; 2015.

guideline.name: FDA drug safety communication — NSAIDs from 20 weeks of pregnancy
guideline.section: Avoid NSAIDs from about 20 weeks of pregnancy (fetal renal dysfunction, oligohydramnios)
guideline.citation: US Food and Drug Administration. Drug Safety Communication, 15 October 2020.

guideline.name: NICE NG25 — Preterm labour and birth
guideline.section: Maternal corticosteroids offered between 24+0 and 33+6 weeks when preterm birth is suspected, diagnosed, established or planned
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Preterm labour and birth (NG25). London: NICE; 2015 (updated 2022).

rationale: Permutation: emergency laparotomy in the third trimester. Tests the obstetric involvement, pregnancy flag, NSAID exclusion, VTE prophylaxis, left uterine displacement, antenatal steroids and imaging choice.
